paper: Longstaff and Schwartz (2001), Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach
canonical_dataset: Published Tables 1 and 2; distinct schemas within one authoritative bundle.

original_source_record.title: Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach
original_source_record.verification: Transcribed from extracted PDF text and visually checked against a rendering of journal page 127.
original_source_record.printed_precision: All reported prices and standard errors are rounded to 0.001 in the original table.

protocol.stock_process: Risk-neutral geometric Brownian motion with constant rate and volatility, zero dividends.
protocol.regressors: Constant, exp(-x/2), exp(-x/2)*(1-x), exp(-x/2)*(1-2*x+x*x/2), with x=S/K.
protocol.regression_sample: Only in-the-money paths at each exercise date.
protocol.regression_target: Future realized cashflow, discounted to the regression date; stock and cashflows normalized by strike for fitting.
protocol.valuation: In-sample stopping-rule fit and valuation; discount actual realized stopped cashflows to time zero and average.
protocol.early_exercise_value: Simulated American value minus the closed-form Black-Scholes European value; no European control variate is stated for Table 1.
protocol.finite_difference_reference: Published implicit finite difference results, 40000 time steps per year and 1000 stock-price steps, compared with explicit finite difference results.
unreported_details: The paper does not publish its random-number generator, seeds, or normal-generation algorithm.
The paper does not state the standard-error calculation formula; its antithetic convention cannot be claimed exactly from the text.
The finite difference stock-domain bounds and complete numerical boundary implementation are not specified in Section 3.
A separately computed CRR tree is an additional numerical reference, not a reproduction of the paper's finite difference implementation.

original_source_record.paper: Longstaff and Schwartz (2001), Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach
original_source_record.verification: Transcribed and visually checked against the original PDF table.
original_source_record.protocol: Eight contracts (S=36 or 44, sigma=.20 or .40, T=1 or 2); five initial seeds each; 100000 in-sample paths and a separate 100000 out-of-sample paths, each with 50000 antithetic pairs; frozen in-sample regression coefficients; K=40, r=.06, 50 exercise dates/year.
original_source_record.printed_precision: Prices, SEs and differences are printed to .001.
original_source_record.known_printed_inconsistency: S=36, sigma=.20, T=2, replicate 3 prints a difference of +.009 although the printed prices 4.820 minus 4.829 give -.009. The CSV preserves the printed sign without silently correcting it.
original_source_record.limitations: Original seeds, RNG and SE formula are unreported. Replicate numbers identify printed rows; they do not identify our new seed values. Compare distributions and aggregate results, not paired original/random-seed rows.
